issues.description: Entire compiled script content is shipped through the compile_notebook RPC response instead of fetched on demand.
issues.detail: The backend already returns pipeline_package_path. Bolting full script_content onto every compile response wastes memory and bandwidth on a payload only used when the user clicks download, and duplicates state that already lives on disk. Add a dedicated download endpoint that reads the file by path, or have the frontend fetch on click.

issues.description: open(script_path) has no explicit encoding and no error handling after a successful compile.
issues.detail: If the script file is missing, unreadable, or non-utf8 under the user's locale, an IOError propagates out of compile_notebook and poisons the entire RPC after the real compilation work succeeded. Specify encoding='utf-8' and either guard the read or remove it entirely in favor of a separate download path.

issues.description: Download icon renders unconditionally but click handler silently no-ops when content is missing.
issues.detail: handleDownloadClick guards on compiledPath && compiledContent and returns silently on failure, while the icon is rendered in the success branch regardless. With an older backend or partial response the user clicks and nothing happens with no feedback. Gate rendering on compiledContent or show a disabled state instead of silent no-op clicks.

issues.description: compiledPath and compiledContent are drilled through multiple React layers when one would suffice.
issues.detail: Both pieces of state thread through DeployProgressState, DeploysProgress, DeployProgress, and Commands purely to feed a Blob at click time. compiledPath is used only to derive a filename via split('/').pop(). Keep the path alone and fetch content on click, eliminating the prop-drilling and arbitrary-sized file bodies sitting in component state.

issues.description: GetAppIcon is used as a click target instead of a real button or anchor.
issues.detail: The SVG icon has onClick and titleAccess but no button semantics, no keyboard handler, and no focus ring. The adjacent 'Done' control is an anchor for a reason. Wrap in IconButton or use <a download> with an object URL to match the surrounding code and provide keyboard access.

issues.description: Filename derivation via split('/').pop() with hardcoded fallback is brittle and contradicts the success contract.
issues.detail: If compiledPath ends with a slash or is empty, the fallback substitutes a fabricated 'pipeline.kale.py' that differs from the actual artifact. Either compiledPath is guaranteed non-empty here (then the fallback is dead code) or it is not (then the user gets a wrong filename). Use a proper basename helper and resolve the contract.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK with a clear root cause: wrong data shape. All three reviewers agree the backend should not ship full script content through the compile RPC response when a path already exists — a dedicated download endpoint or on-click fetch is the correct composition. The file read also lacks encoding and post-success error handling, so an IOError silently fails the whole compile. On the frontend, content and path are prop-drilled through four layers, the download icon lacks button semantics and keyboard access, and the click handler silently no-ops when content is missing. The feature intent is right; strip script_content from the RPC, add a streaming download route, and use proper button/anchor primitives.
